extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of art history, painters, and conservators interested in Italian Renaissance art and architecture
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting criteria and standards used in Vasari's biographies to judge Renaissance painters, sculptors, and architects — e.g., draughtsmanship, invention, colour, composition, durability of buildings, fidelity to literary/iconographic sources, and technique. Useful for assessing or producing period-appropriate frescoes, panels, and civic architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draughtsmanship (drawing skill)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simone was not very excellent in draughtsmanship
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text notes draughtsmanship as an identifiable quality: some masters are praised or faulted specifically for their drawing ability. Example: Simone 'was not very excellent in draughtsmanship' though he had other strengths; contrast is used to evaluate overall mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention from nature (originality inspired by nature)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari values invention drawn from observing nature — original compositions and ideas derived from life. Simone is praised for 'invention from nature' even when his draughtsmanship was weaker; inventive power can compensate for technical faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portraiture from life / likeness accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: He took much delight in drawing portraits from the life; in this he was held... the greatest master of his times
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate likenesses and life-portraits are singled out as a major virtue; portraiture 'from the life' is repeatedly noted as a mark of excellence (e.g., Petrarca, Madonna Laura). Portraits of contemporaries in frescoes used as evidence of skill and documentary value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freshness and vivacity of colour (colouring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Taddeo... made [the colouring] fresher and more vivacious than that of Giotto
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour handling is a distinct evaluative axis: fresher, more vivacious colouring is praised. Durability and brightness of pigments (see Orcagna's façade colours preserved vividly) are also noted as marks of technical excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression of emotion and liveliness
rubrics_metrics.description: expressing supplication, joy, sorrow, and other similar emotions; figures with vivid expressions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to convey emotions (supplication, joy, sorrow, rage, hope, fear) and 'liveliness' in faces and attitudes is repeatedly praised as central to a successful narrative painting (e.g., soldiers and horses doubting whether they have crucified Christ; vivid expressions of rage in Passion scenes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and narrative arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: a very large work ... containing the Coronation of Our Lady, with an infinity of figures ... many horses and soldiers in beautiful attitudes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation attends to overall composition and the clear telling of a story across many figures: arrangement, hierarchy, clarity of episodes, and the ability to manage complex multi-figure narratives (chapel cycles, Last Supper, Judgment scenes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Depiction of movement and animated action
rubrics_metrics.description: many horses and soldiers in beautiful attitudes, which they are striking with various animated movements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capturing animated poses, the movement of figures and animals, and dynamic interactions (e.g., throwing dice, pulling with ropes, storm-tossed boats) is a positive quality; reviewers note naturalistic and convincing motion as evidence of mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate rendering of natural phenomena and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: complete understanding of the tempestuous agitation of the sea and of the fury of the storm
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convincing depiction of environment, weather, sea, landscape and their physical effects on people and objects is praised (e.g., boats in storms, rocky crags, cities as light sources). Such understanding enhances realism and narrative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fresco technique and use of cartoons (working method)
rubrics_metrics.description: outlined with the brush in red over the plaster, as may still be seen to-day; which method of working was the cartoon that our old masters used to make for painting in fresco
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari describes technical workshop practices — preparatory cartoons, red brush outlines on fresh plaster — as standard methods for speed and correctness in fresco. Technique and adherence to established methods matter to the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to complete and imitate another master's unfinished work faithfully
rubrics_metrics.description: Lippo afterwards finished many works that Simone had left imperfect, and among these ... wherein Lippo finished what Simone had begun, imitating that which the said Simone had made
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skill in finishing another painter's incomplete work while imitating their manner is presented as a professional virtue — preserving continuity of style and respecting original design when completing commissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iconographic appropriateness and allegorical clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: On the wall below are the Seven Sciences, with their names and with those figures below them that are appropriate to each
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct identification and apt representation of allegorical and symbolic figures (Sciences, Virtues, Theological and Cardinal Virtues) and matching them to appropriate attributes and subsidiary figures is an explicit criterion for a successful complex program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of light for spiritual effect
rubrics_metrics.description: he wished to attempt to make the splendour of the Glorified Body give forth light
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manipulation of light to convey divinity or spiritual radiance (e.g., the Glorified Body emitting light) is an artistic aim; Vasari notes experiments and the difficulty of sustaining such effects across a composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of contemporary and notable figures (portrait-integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: he portrayed Cimabue, the architect Lapo, his son Arnolfo, and himself... he portrayed Benedetto XI of Treviso... portraits from the life... portraits of Clement V, Pope Clement VI
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrating portraits of patrons, popes, poets, and civic figures within narrative cycles is valued; these likenesses serve documentary, political, and commemorative functions and are a mark of the painter's skill in portraiture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and use of inscriptions, verses, and textual elements
rubrics_metrics.description: filled this whole work of his with such writings... with these verses below... round these dead bodies are some devils who are tearing their souls from their mouths
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inscriptions and verses incorporated into painted work (captions, scrolls, poetic lines) are discussed as part of the artistic program; their placement, legibility, and appropriateness contribute to the work's meaning and taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versatility across media (multi-disciplinary competence)
rubrics_metrics.description: painter, sculptor, architect, and poet... began while still a child to give attention to sculpture under Andrea Pisano... he applied himself to drawing... painting... sculpture... architecture
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari admires artists competent in multiple related disciplines; ability to work across painting, sculpture, and architecture is treated as evidence of a universal intellect and practical advantage (designing buildings as well as decoration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithfulness to authoritative literary/descriptive sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Hell, with the abysses, centres, and other things described by Dante, of whom Andrea was an ardent student
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a painted program is based on a literary model (Dante), fidelity to that source's descriptions and successful translation into visual terms are treated positively; incorporation of literary learning is prestigious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish quality and preservation (technical finish and longevity)
rubrics_metrics.description: these works... were finished to perfection... colours in that exposed place have been preserved marvellously vivid and beautiful up to our own day
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree of finish ('finished to perfection') and the long-term preservation of pigments and surfaces are noted as measures of technical success. Durability under exposure and resistance to weathering are important for façade and public works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural strength, engineering, and material workmanship in architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: made it with such strength in the piers and with such magnificence in the arches, all of stone squared with the chisel... it supports to-day twenty-two shops on either side... it was not moved in the year 1557 by that which threw down other bridges
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Architectural evaluation emphasizes solidity of foundations and piers, quality of masonry ('stones squared with the chisel'), durability against floods, and the capacity to combine structural soundness with aesthetic magnificence. Economic and civic utility (shops, rents) are also part of the appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craftsmanship, ornament, and cost-effectiveness in building projects
rubrics_metrics.description: stones could not be put together with more diligence, nor could a more beautiful tower be made, with regard either to ornament, or cost, or design
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment includes the quality of craftwork, ornamental treatment, adherence to budget or reasonable cost, and success of overall design — excellence is measured across aesthetics, construction quality, and prudent expense.
